[← All agentic coding exercises](exercises.qmd)

**Start:** a finished project on farm trade and farm support, built by a team of four analysts.
It has R, Python and Stata code, clean data, results and five months of Git history.
You open it in Positron or VS Code, with an AI assistant: Posit Assistant, Claude Code or Copilot Chat.

**Target:** you can explain what the project does and how to run it.
You have run one part of it, fixed one chart and added one new result, with the AI doing the typing.

[Download the project (.zip)](files/farm-trade-support.zip){.btn .btn-primary}

It unzips to `farm-trade-support/`, with a hidden `.git` folder that holds the history.
Copy the prompts on this page into the assistant one at a time.

**Data sources:** farm trade from the [FAOSTAT Detailed Trade Matrix](https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/TM) (FAO, CC BY 4.0).
Distance, borders, language and trade agreements from the [CEPII Gravity database](https://www.cepii.fr/CEPII/en/bdd_modele/bdd_modele_item.asp?id=8), V202211 (Etalab Open Licence 2.0).
The subsidy data in `farm_support.csv` are **synthetic**: a computer made them up, with known true values.

## Before you start

- **Software:** Python with `pandas` and `matplotlib` is enough. R with `fixest` and Stata are optional.
  See [Install the software](../intro/software-setup.qmd).
- **No Stata?** Read the Stata results in `outputs/`, which are committed.
  Ask the AI to explain `code/03_sem.do`, or to rewrite it in R or Python.
  Exercise 3 (coming soon) builds on that.
- **Assistant:** use agent mode, so the AI can read files and run commands.
  The project has an [instructions file](../agentic/agentic.qmd#ide-ai), `AGENTS.md`, which all three assistants read.
- **Approvals:** the AI explains its plan and asks before it changes files or runs a command. Click the approve button in the chat, or reply "yes".
- **Time:** about 45 minutes for steps 1 to 6 and the comparison, reading included. The bonus is optional and takes about 10 more.

## Step 1. Look around without AI (6 min)

Unzip the file. In Positron or VS Code, open the folder `farm-trade-support/` (**File > Open Folder**).
Read `README.md`. Try to run one script in a language you know.

**What you should see:** folders `data/`, `code/`, `outputs/` and `reports/`, and one master script per language in `code/`.
Running a script may fail. That is fine: step 2 fixes it.

**Watch for:** where the results go, and which files you must not edit by hand (the README says).

## Step 2. Ask the AI what the project is and how to run it (6 min)

``` text
Explain this project to me in plain words: what question each part answers,
which language it uses, which data it reads and where its results go.
Then tell me the exact command to run the Python part from the project root,
and check that I have what it needs. Do not change any file yet.
```

If your run in step 1 failed, paste the error into the chat, then send:

``` text
Why did this fail, and how do I fix it? Explain each step before you run it.
```

**What you should see:** three parts (Python bloc charts, R gravity model, Stata subsidy model), the command `python code/00_master.py`, and a warning that the subsidy data are synthetic.

**Watch for:** an AI that changes or installs anything before you agree, and claims about files it has not opened.

## Step 3. Run it and open the results (4 min)

``` text
Run the Python part of the project. Then list every figure and table in
outputs/, with the script that makes each one. Do not change any file.
```

**What you should see:** `Done. Results are in outputs/.` in the terminal, and a list of figures and tables.
Open two of the figures in the editor.

**Watch for:** files listed that are not in `outputs/`, and a script named for a figure it does not make.

## Step 4. Explain the results (8 min)

``` text
Explain in three sentences what the R gravity table and the Stata elasticities
in outputs/data/sem_effects.csv say. Then write a short note of about 150 words
on the main results in reports/results-note.md. Use only numbers from files in
outputs/, and name the file each number comes from.
```

**What you should see:** a plain explanation, and a new file in `reports/`.
Check two numbers in the note against the files it names.

**Watch for:** numbers that are in no file, causal words such as "drives" or "causes" for the gravity results, and Stata results discussed without saying the data are synthetic.

## Step 5. Fix the trend chart (8 min)

Open `outputs/figures/bloc_trend.png`. Then ask:

``` text
Look at outputs/figures/bloc_trend.png and the script that makes it.
What would you improve so a reader understands the chart at a glance?
List the problems first. Then fix them in the script, rerun it, and tell
me what you changed.
```

**What you should see:** a list of problems, a changed `code/02_bloc_trend.py`, and a clearer chart.
Did the AI miss something you would fix? Ask for it.

**Watch for:** a chart edited by hand or saved under a new name, and changes to `outputs/data/bloc_trade.csv`, which other tools read.

## Step 6. Add a new result: two blocs side by side (8 min)

``` text
Add a new figure: two panels side by side, one for the farm exports of the
EU and one for Mercosur, with one line per destination bloc. Use trade in
USD billions. Put it in a new script, code/04_bloc_panel.py, that reads
outputs/data/bloc_trade.csv and saves outputs/figures/bloc_panel_eu_mercosur.png.
Add the script to code/00_master.py, run it, and describe what the panels show.
```

**What you should see:** a new script, one new line in `code/00_master.py`, and a new figure in `outputs/figures/`.
Pick other blocs if you like: the six are EU, USMCA, Mercosur, ASEAN, East Asia and Oceania.

**Watch for:** a new package added without asking, an absolute path in the script, and a script missing from `code/00_master.py`.

## Bonus. See what changed and who did what (+10 min, optional)

**With Git:** open the **Source Control** view (`Ctrl+Shift+G`). Click each changed file to see its diff. Then ask:

``` text
Summarise the Git history of this project: who worked on what, on which
branches, when the branches were merged, and why the main changes were made.
Then list the files I changed today that are not committed yet.
```

**Without Git:** open a script you changed, go to the **Explorer** view (`Ctrl+Shift+E`) and expand **Timeline** at the bottom.
Each save, by you or the AI, is an entry. Click one to compare it with the current file. This works in VS Code and in Positron.

**What you should see:** four analysts, separate R, Stata and Python branches merged into `main` at different times, a data fix, and your own changes listed as not committed.

**Watch for:** a history summary with names or dates that are not in the log.

## Compare with the target (5 min)

- [Corrected trend chart](files/expected/bloc_trend_fixed.png)
- [Side-by-side panel for the EU and Mercosur](files/expected/bloc_panel_eu_mercosur.png)
- [Results note](files/expected/results-note.md)
- [Code changes for steps 5 and 6 (.diff)](files/expected/bloc-charts.diff)

Your charts will look different. What matters is that each one has a source script, and you can rerun it.

**Discuss:** Which flaw did the AI miss? Would you trust its note without checking the numbers?

## Answer key: try the steps first

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the answers"}

**Step 4.** Key numbers: distance elasticity -0.57; trade agreement coefficient 0.62, so pairs with an agreement trade about 85% more. This is an association, not a causal effect.
The Stata estimates are 0.105 direct, 0.238 indirect and 0.342 total, close to the true 0.10, 0.24 and 0.34.
See the [results note](files/expected/results-note.md).

**Step 5.** The original chart has three flaws:

1. The title is misspelled: "Farm trade betwen blocs".
2. All 36 bloc pairs are on one chart, so the lines and the legend cannot be read.
3. The y-axis is in raw dollars, with numbers up to 200,000,000,000.

One fix: correct the title, keep only the 8 largest flows in 2019, and show USD billions.
Small multiples or a log scale are also fine.

Other valid finds: the legend hides the last years, colours repeat across 36 lines, and the x-axis has no 2019 tick. The reference fix leaves the missing 2019 tick as it is.

![Corrected trend chart](files/expected/bloc_trend_fixed.png){fig-alt="Line chart of the 8 largest farm trade flows between blocs, 2000 to 2019, in USD billions. Trade inside the EU is the largest, rising from about 77 to 219 billion."}

**Step 6.** Mercosur's main market moved from the EU to East Asia around 2010.
Its exports to East Asia grew from USD 2.7 billion in 2000 to 43.9 billion in 2019.
Each panel has its own y-axis, because EU trade is much larger.

![EU and Mercosur farm exports by destination bloc](files/expected/bloc_panel_eu_mercosur.png){fig-alt="Two line charts side by side. Left: EU farm exports by destination bloc, dominated by trade inside the EU. Right: Mercosur farm exports, where East Asia overtakes the EU around 2010."}
:::
